title: Port Mahon Rising
premise: In 1798, Mirabel Crane carries sealed dispatches for a republic on the edge of collapse, measuring her loyalty in ounces and hours. When a stranger named Elias Vane arrives in Port Mahon bearing letters written in the hand of her brother — officially dead, now branded an enemy agent — she must decide whether family is blood or promise. Their uneasy alliance becomes love as they race to deliver a peace proposal before the century turns and war makes traitors of them both. In the end, Mirabel burns the orders that would doom the harbor town, keeps her peacetime promise at the cost of her commission, and chooses exile with Elias over survival within a state that no longer deserves her.
about_author: Mara Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing naval correspondence from the Mediterranean campaigns. She writes from a stone house overlooking a harbor much like Port Mahon, where she first found a courier's ledger annotated in two hands.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Mirabel Crane, POV. In a besieged port city, Mirabel catalogs her diplomatic dispatches by weight and burn-time, establishing her creed: carry little, trust less. She receives final orders for Port Mahon. Emotional beat: disciplined detachment masking grief for a brother reported dead at sea.

chapters.title: Last Sailing of the Season
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Aboard a leaky brig with forged papers sewn into her coat lining, she endures a storm and a suspicious purser who counts her trunks twice. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into focus; she memorizes and destroys one cipher key as insurance against capture.

chapters.title: Port Mahon
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. She arrives in the limestone harbor city, delivers credentials to Consul Aubert, and notes the garrison's decay and the townsfolk's wary hospitality. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being trusted by everyone and known by no one.

chapters.title: A Stranger's Hand
chapters.summary: Elias Vane, POV. A smuggler-turned-messenger lands at night carrying letters he was paid never to read — addressed in handwriting Mirabel will recognize. He observes her receiving them and watches her composure crack. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into complicity; he realizes what he carries is worth lives.

chapters.title: Dead Men Write Neatly
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Alone, she verifies the impossible: her brother Tomas, declared drowned, has written from enemy territory asking her to meet him at the old windmill. Emotional beat: hope arriving like contraband — thrilling, dangerous, deniable.

chapters.title: Terms of Carriage
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Mirabel confronts Elias; he admits he was hired by an intermediary he never met and offers to guide her to the windmill for a price. They strike a wary bargain. Emotional beat: two professionals negotiating trust neither can afford.

chapters.title: The Windmill Road
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. The journey inland through olive terraces; conversation strips away their cover stories layer by layer. Elias reveals he once carried mail between her family and Tomas in peacetime — the promise he made then binds him now. Emotional beat: reluctant intimacy kindling.

chapters.title: What the Mill Remembered
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. At the ruined windmill they find not Tomas but his sealed confession and a map: he is alive, held as leverage by a faction that wants the consul's dispatches. Emotional beat: relief and fury braided together; the trap was aimed at her all along.

chapters.title: The Consul's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Back in Port Mahon, she discovers Consul Aubert is playing both sides, trading the harbor's neutrality for his own passage out. Emotional beat: disillusionment — the republic she serves is already sold.

chapters.title: Salt and Cipher
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias decodes part of Tomas's confession using a childhood cipher only the Crane siblings knew, proving his identity beyond doubt. He and Mirabel plan extraction. Emotional beat: Elias crossing from hired hand to committed ally, aware of what that will cost.

chapters.title: An Enemy Declared
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Official word arrives: Tomas Crane is formally listed as an enemy agent, and aiding him is treason. Aubert quietly suggests Mirabel prove her loyalty by luring her brother into custody. Emotional beat: duty and love become openly incompatible.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Elias is recognized by an old smuggling rival now working for Aubert, who offers him immunity to betray Mirabel. He refuses, burns his own safe-conduct papers. Emotional beat: the moment a mercenary becomes a man with something to lose.

chapters.title: Night Signals
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Using harbor lantern codes, Mirabel signals Tomas's captors to negotiate an exchange: herself for her brother. Elias argues against it; they quarrel bitterly. Emotional beat: love expressed as argument, each trying to be the one who pays.

chapters.title: The Exchange at Cala Figuera
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. The swap goes wrong — Aubert's soldiers ambush the cove. Tomas appears at last, wounded but alive, and fights beside them. Emotional beat: reunion amid gunfire; three siblings' worth of history compressed into minutes.

chapters.title: Brother, Stranger, Enemy
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Hiding in a fisherman's cellar, Tomas explains why he defected: he discovered the republic planned to sacrifice Port Mahon as a bargaining chip. Emotional beat: Mirabel's world reordering — the traitor is the honest one.

chapters.title: Orders to Burn
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. She reads her own sealed orders at last: deliver the dispatches that authorize the harbor's abandonment and its defenders' arrest. Emotional beat: cold clarity; she holds the instrument of the town's destruction in her hands.

chapters.title: Century's Edge
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. New Year's Eve, 1799. The faction closes in; Aubert offers Mirabel a final chance to comply and be spared. Elias prepares escape boats while the town celebrates above them, oblivious. Emotional beat: dread and tenderness on the last night of the old world.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. At midnight she feeds the dispatches to the consulate stove, keeping only Tomas's confession as evidence. Aubert's men storm in; Elias and Tomas hold the courtyard. Emotional beat: liberation through arson — she finally weighs less than her conscience.

chapters.title: The Harbor Gate
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. The flight to the boats through burning signal fires; Tomas takes a bullet covering Mirabel, insisting they leave him if needed. They refuse. Emotional beat: the promise made in peacetime honored under fire, at full price.

chapters.title: Open Water
chapters.summary: Elias, POV. Aboard a small cutter bound for neutral waters, pursued briefly then lost in fog. Tomas feverish below decks; Mirabel steering. Emotional beat: exhaustion softened by the strange calm of having nothing left to protect but each other.

chapters.title: Exile's Coast
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. Landfall on a neutral shore; Tomas recovers enough to walk. Mirabel writes a final report she will never send, then burns it too. Emotional beat: mourning her country without regretting her choice.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Elias, alternating. One year later, running a modest shipping office under new names, they receive word that Port Mahon's defenders were freed after the burned orders could not be verified. On the quay, Mirabel measures the world again — this time finding it light. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not assigned; love that survived its price.
